newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt rounds up 41 suspected Moslem militants.
newsitem.headline: Egypt rounds up 41 suspected Moslem militants.

text.p: Egyptian security forces have rounded up 41 men they suspect of belonging to the Moslem militant group Jihad, security sources said on Saturday.
They said police captured the Islamists in the Cairo and Sharqiya provinces after identifying and tracking them down in nine countries.
Police say the 41 members had been living abroad either as political refugees or as aid workers and met in Egypt to gather funds or try to recruit new members, the sources said.
Several had received special military training in Afghanistan and had held religious classes in Egypt where they taught their militant brand of Islam.

Members of Jihad, which is led by fugitive medical doctor Ayman al-Zawahri, gunned down President Anwar Sadat in 1981 while he was watching a military parade. The group is believed to be behind a wave of bomb attacks and assassination attempts over the past four years.

Like the Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group), Jihad is fighting to transform Egypt into a strict Islamic state. More than 1,000 people have been killed since the political violence erupted in Egypt in 1992 and recent government crackdowns have largely contained the militants' activities.
Government newspapers published pictures of 11 men they say are leading Jihad members and the sources said the men would be held for investigation.
